RI-FMW-005 covers employment service IT staffing, and this is the agency's own IT headcount. The text makes no link to EU networks, as the note says, so only chain use is possible. The same sentence recurs across the report series: rule once (also MKD-GOV-2024-005-0008, MKD-GOV-2025-003-0015, MKD-GOV-2026-001-0009).

R21 excludes cybercrime enforcement; this is national CSIRT incident data, and the neighbouring items 0017 to 0019 and 0021 are under RI-TEC-023. The note's test, security of public institutions, is not in the theme definition. Against: the targets are citizens, not state systems. See also MKD-GOV-2022-003-0007.

Same point as MKD-GOV-2023-002-0042, and stronger on framing: the measure is in the action plan of the national ICT strategy, and sector tools qualify when framed as digital transformation of government. RI-TEC-004 is the alternative. Rule on e-Inspector once.

Incident response capacity is in the TECH-CYBER definition and the rules do not limit it to civil systems. The note relies on the national law, which does make its provisions non-mandatory for defence bodies. A reasonable line, but it is one for the analyst to confirm as a group.

The claim is literally about protecting networks and information systems, so saying it fails materiality is weak; the sound ground is that the law excludes accredited classified systems (Art. 5(5), checked). A single register for social insurance is close to the TECH-DATA example of setting up a register, and RI-TEC-015 covers institutional registers. The note is right that the text describes no data system, and no Chapter 2 link is stated. Also applies to MKD-GOV-2025-003-0012.
